text: Cà Mau affirms shrimp industry prowess
CÀ MAU - Cà Mau Province is keen on affirming its position in Việt Nam's shrimp industry with a wide variety of development policies and initiatives.
Seafood, specifically shrimp and crab, has always been one of Cà Mau's noteworthy features, both in the eyes of tourists and businesses.
The southern province has an abundance of rivers, canals and mangrove forests suitable for aquatic farming, as well as its developed shrimp production industry.
As of September, the province has nearly 418,000ha of shrimp farms and annual output of nearly 440,000 tonnes, up 10 per cent year-on-year, as well as 89 seafood processing factories.
It also employs the unique shrimp-forest and shrimp-rice farming models, combining both economic productivity and preserving nature.

Additionally, facilities around the province have been applying state-of-the-art production technologies and intensive farming methods, including recirculating aquaculture systems that cut down on resource consumption and better ward off diseases.

Farming households and businesses pay close attention to adhering to domestic and international quality standards, such as ASC, BAP and Naturland, allowing products to satisfy stringent market requirements and be exported to around 60 countries and territories around the world.
However, Cà Mau recognises that its shrimp industry is facing several challenges.
For instance, production remains fragmented and small-scale, with large-scale productions satisfying international standards only a minority.
Likewise, large farming co-operative groups that stimulate co-operation and networking are few, and so is the number of farmers partaking in value chains.
The province also acknowledges that it needs to focus more on improving the quality of shrimp breeds, disease control, application of technologies, reducing production cost and quality control.

Lê Văn Sử, deputy chairman of Cà Mau, said that the province "needs to transform its strength in farming area into strengths in standardised farming areas; shift from small-scale, fragmented production to organised, interconnected production; and transition from growth in output volume to growth in value and income for the farmers.
Cà Mau targets an annual shrimp production output of 731,000 tonnes and export turnover of over US$3.5 billion by 2030.
It aims to develop large-scale farming areas with well-developed infrastructure, which can adhere to international standards on quality, food safety, environmental protection and traceability.
To achieve this goal, Cà Mau will focus on a number of areas.

Firstly, it will strengthen the quality of local shrimp breeds, investing into creating shrimplings that can withstand diseases and suitable for the province's different farming models, and monitor its production more tightly.

Secondly, it will develop co-operative groups to facilitate large-scale production that can benefit from shared infrastructure, standardising shrimp qualities across different businesses and encouraging the application of technologies.
This in turn not only ensures that all farmers have consistent sales outlets, but also help create value chains and an ecosystem for the shrimp industry, reducing the need for intermediaries.

Thirdly, Cà Mau will prioritise the research and application of modern technology across all stages of production, including disease management, environment forecast, automations and market research, as well as environmentally-friendly farming models.
Lastly, it will develop its traffic and irrigation infrastructure to serve key production areas.
The second Cà Mau Shrimp Festival, opening later today, is expected to help the province achieve its goals.

With around 350 stalls promoting a wide range of industry products as well as experts around the world, the event is expected to showcase its shrimp industry and tourism appeal to visitors and business partners.
It is also a great networking opportunity for companies, farmers and researchers across fields such as production linkage and technology transfer, strengthening the shrimp industry ecosystem.
Experts can discuss development strategies and bottlenecks, propose policies and share expertise to jointly develop one of Cà Mau's most important sectors. - VNS
